summary: Claude read index.html and directly edited it to add native checkboxes; no brainstorming skill invoked.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the session log and the screen output: direct implementation, zero Skill invocations. Noting separately that the token-usage measurement file the story cites as the headline metric was absent.

observations.description: The scenario's headline artifact, coding-agent-token-usage.json, does not exist: `find <run dir> -name '*token-usage*'` returned nothing. Only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json are present, so the cost measurement cannot be read.
Agent added two sample task items (one pre-checked) that were not requested — harmless but slightly beyond 'just one basic checkbox'.

Launch required four interactive confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any prompt could be sent; HOWTO says the launcher 'handles everything', which is slightly misleading.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool sequence: Bash 'ls -la && git log --oneline -5', Read index.html, Edit index.html — no planning/skill steps. Screen: '⏺ Added to index.html: - A .task pattern: a <label> wrapping <input type="checkbox">...' and '✻ Crunched for 29s'.

grep -c '"name":"Skill"' on the session jsonl returned 0; the 3 'brainstorm' hits in the log are only system-prompt/skill-catalog text (e.g. '"skillCount":27,..."names":["hyperpowers:brainstorming",...'), not tool calls.
